candidates.text: Raw Materials: Diego Delgado-Elias Drawn to historic buildings and the traces they carry, Peruvian designer and architect Diego Delgado-Elias has spent his 20-year career reinforcing the elements that develop a space’s warmth and character. Based in Paris, his architecture and interior design studio expands this affinity for creating lived-in spaces that seem to have accumulated naturally over time, observing the lives that occupied a house before him – left as marks on walls, layers of paint, or objects that appear frozen and unmoved. - Daniel Guix While working to restore a seventeenth-century house in the Provençal village of Visan, France, Delgado-Elias found a place that quietly mirrors his sentimental understanding and way of looking at spaces. Moving between past and present, the house becomes an echo of other spaces and sensations that remain with him, while bearing the influence of the surrounding nature in its preserved frescoes, original materials, and domestic objects. For a new short documentary, director Daniel Guix studies Delgado-Elias’ world through the house, exploring how our earliest encounters with spaces can mold our sensibility. Shooting on 16mm, to capture the grain, movement and texture of memory, Guix brings Delgado-Elias’ reflections into conversation with the house, as a rhythm that connects one room to the next, and a reminder of the formative impressions that unconsciously shape creative vision.
candidates.title: Raw Materials: Diego Delgado-Elias
